# Solid para-hydrogen reference phase state

`eos.parahydrogen_solid_phase`

## Source

**Sannerhaugen, A. (2026)**

The fundamental Helmholtz equation for solid para-hydrogen, evaluated in temperature and molar volume and differentiated to second order by forward automatic differentiation.


## Algorithm

A model rather than a calculation: what this page pins down is the procedure,
not an equation, and both implementations read it from here.

| Setting | Value |
|---|---|
| Scheme | `bracketed_log_volume_newton` |
| Convergence | `absolute` |
| Tolerance | `1e-10` |
| Max iterations | `100` |
| Initialisation | `zero_pressure_volume` |

## Inputs

| Name | Unit | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `T` | K | absolute temperature |
| `P` | Pa | absolute pressure |


## Outputs

| Name | Unit | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `z_factor` | dimensionless | the compressibility factor `Z = P v/(R T)` |
| `u` | J/mol | the internal energy |
| `h` | J/mol | the enthalpy |
| `s` | J/(mol*K) | the entropy |
| `cv` | J/(mol*K) | the isochoric heat capacity |
| `cp` | J/(mol*K) | the isobaric heat capacity |
| `g` | J/mol | the Gibbs energy, `h - T s` |

| Bound | On violation | Why |
|---|---|---|
| `T > 0 and T <= 200` | raises | the published equation is stated for temperatures to 200 K |
| `P > 0 and P <= 1e+10` | raises | the published equation is stated for pressures to 10 GPa |

## Assumptions

- the phase is solid hcp phase-I para-hydrogen; the equation of state is the Sannerhaugen fundamental Helmholtz formulation of NeqSim's `thermo.util.solid.ParaHydrogenSolidHelmholtzEquation`, a Vinet cold curve with Debye, Einstein and internal-vibration terms.
- the molar volume is solved from the pressure by bracketing and bisection/Newton in logarithmic volume, so the solid root is the one selected.
- every property follows from the second-order Helmholtz derivatives, computed by one forward automatic-differentiation pass rather than per-term derivative transcriptions.
- the gas constant is the thesis equation's own `R = 8.3144621` J/(mol.K).
